headline: The new HRRR run shows one isolated 1.16 in downpour hour around 1 AM Wednesday that no independent model supports; the other models trended even drier, so the consensus stays far below street-flooding amounts, but the overnight hours deserve a watch.

summary.text: HRRR jumped from 0.15 to 1.30 in for its wettest 3 hours, almost all from one 1.16 in hour around 1 AM Wednesday. Treated as a low-confidence shower cell, not a trend.
NBM fell from 0.11 to 0.04 in and ECMWF from 0.08 to 0.01 in. RRFS unchanged at 0.08 in. Consensus down from 0.11 to 0.08 in.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: HRRR 1.30, GFS 1.24 (copies HRRR's spike hour exactly, not independent), RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.04, ECMWF 0.01 in. HRRR is the lone outlier.
No street flooding on the consensus (0.08 in, the rating card's number). If HRRR's burst verified it would be far past Purple (1.26 in), so watch overnight Tuesday.
Dry today and Tuesday daytime. Light rain about 7 to 11 PM Tuesday in most models. HRRR's possible downpour around 1 AM Wednesday; light rain ends by early Wednesday morning.
Evening rain falls near the -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM Tuesday. HRRR's 1 AM cell would hit the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, running about 1.4 ft above prediction. Channel low: 0.13 ft.
Today (NWS says it too): clear street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags. Before bed Tuesday, move cars out of the cul-de-sac as a precaution and keep the page open.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The calm before the storm: dry today and tonight as a ridge builds east, with high clouds streaming in. NWS San Francisco (7:06 AM update) calls today the day to clear storm drains and gutters ahead of a moderate rain and wind storm Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday morning, as a shortwave trough and cold front cross Northern California. NWS rain totals are unchanged since its 1:25 AM forecast: 0.4 to 1.0 in for the San Francisco Peninsula and 0.15 to 0.5 in for the East and South Bays, with wiggle room either way depending on the low's track. Winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph near the coast and through gaps. A general thunder risk (heavy downpours possible with any storm that forms), best north of the Golden Gate. Dry Thanksgiving and Friday; wet weather favored for the weekend. The Coastal Flood Warning for the Bay shoreline is now in effect.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
The models split this morning. Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 7 AM Monday to 7 AM Thursday:
• HRRR (5 AM Mon run, now reaches 4 AM Wednesday): 1.30 / 1.55 in, up from 0.15 / 0.15 in. Light rain 10 PM to midnight Tuesday (0.02 to 0.04 in per hour), then a single 1.16 in hour around 1 AM Wednesday, flanked by 0.02 in hours, then 0.13 and 0.16 in around 3 and 4 AM. The 15-minute output ends at 11:45 PM Tuesday and shows only 0.004 to 0.012 in per 15 minutes, so it cannot confirm or rule out the cell.
• GFS: 1.24 / 1.37 in, up from 0.08 / 0.10 in, but its hours from 10 PM Tuesday to 1 AM Wednesday, including the 1.16 in spike, are identical to HRRR's, so it is not independent support.
• RRFS (10 PM Sun run, same as last time): 0.08 / 0.16 in, wettest 8 to 11 PM Tuesday, one 0.06 in hour around 7 AM Wednesday.
• NBM: 0.04 / 0.12 in, down from 0.11 / 0.42 in. Only 0.01 in per hour, 7 to 11 PM Tuesday.
• ECMWF: 0.01 / 0.04 in, down from 0.08 / 0.13 in. Almost dry.

Consensus (HRRR 1.30 × 1.25 = 1.63, RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.04): middle value 0.08 in, down from 0.11 in, so the rating card stays at none. A single HRRR hour more than seven times anything around it, with no support from RRFS, NBM or ECMWF, reads as a low-confidence convective cell rather than a trend; NWS does keep a general thunder risk with the front. Two reasons not to dismiss it: HRRR-type guidance has under-forecast local bursts here by about 3×, and NWS's Peninsula range (0.4 to 1.0 in) is well above every independent model's total for the street. Selecting HRRR only on the dashboard would show this spike; the next few HRRR runs will tell whether it persists.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City (1.0 to 1.7 ft at the lows). This morning's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM runs about 10.6 ft; tonight's 7.0 ft high at 12:16 AM Tuesday about 8.4 ft; Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM about 10.9 ft. Tuesday evening's light rain falls near the predicted -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM, with the model near -0.3 ft at 7 PM and 3.6 ft at 10 PM, so the channel can drain. The timing is worse for HRRR's cell: the model has the water at 7.2 ft at midnight and 8.3 ft at 1 AM Wednesday (its last hour), near the predicted 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, which would slow channel drainage if a downpour hit then. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM comes after all models have the rain over.

NWS: Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines, 6:10 AM Monday to 4 PM Thursday, with up to 2.7 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. San Francisco high tides 2.0 ft above normal today, 2.4 ft Tuesday, 2.7 ft Wednesday and 2.2 ft Thursday, including up to 1.5 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.13 ft at 7 AM, flat between 0.12 and 0.17 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry and calm on the street this morning. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to 5:13 AM. NWS reports dense Tule fog in the interior valleys and high clouds moving in; the Bay shoreline is seeing significant coastal flooding at this morning's high tide.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Tuesday afternoon: dry. Moderate for Tuesday evening: four of five models agree on light rain, wettest 0.01 to 0.08 in per 3 hours. High for overnight Tuesday into Wednesday: HRRR alone (copied by GFS) has a downpour around 1 AM that would be a serious street-flooding burst if real, at the overnight high tide. The key questions are whether later HRRR runs keep the cell, whether RRFS's next run shows anything similar, and whether NWS's higher Peninsula totals or the drier point models verify.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Today and Tuesday morning: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, and check sandbags.
• Tuesday afternoon and evening: gusts to 40 mph possible; outages can slow the pumps.
• Tuesday before bed: as a low-cost precaution against HRRR's overnight cell, move cars out of the cul-de-sac and keep this page open; check the next discussion Tuesday evening.
• If a downpour hits overnight, timestamped photos at the peak help; don't walk or drive through moving water.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the late-morning high tides through Thursday.
